text:
maria: heads up — perf regression spotted on canary (last commit landed on runtime). p95 up ~45% on long-context chat workloads. can we triage?
sam: which workload? microbatch configs or kernel change?
li: logs show a different kernel path being chosen for 2 layers when seq_len > 1024. kernel selector change was in that PR.
maya: we were also testing microbatch size 8 -> 16 yesterday as part of throughput tuning. might be batching interaction.
maria: repro steps: replayed 6 hours of prod recog chat traffic (anonymized) against canary. observed latency tail increase after ~30 mins when KV cache warmed.
perf-bot: nightly-profiling artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/1710624000/canary-profiles.tar.gz
sam: thanks. quick numbers from the replay: baseline (main): p50 78ms p95 210ms p99 430ms throughput 420 req/s. canary: p50 80ms p95 305ms p99 720ms throughput 460 req/s.
li: interesting — throughput up but tail latency worse. indicates different batching/kernels tradeoff.
maya: microbatching heuristic note: we currently increase microbatch size dynamically up to 16 if server CPU < 70% and avg latency < SLO. maybe the heuristic is too aggressive under long sequences.
sam: also kernel selector: fallback to uint8-gemm kernel for some attention sizes; that kernel has worse single-request latency but better throughput. it will be chosen when batch_size >= 8.
maria: key question — do we optimize for overall throughput or keep strict p99 SLO? product wants 300ms p95 SLO for interactive chat.
li: for SRE/P99 we should prefer conservative microbatches: cap at 8 for interactive mode and pin to fp16 kernels. that costs ~10% throughput.
sam: we should validate with both synthetic cpu-bound load and real replay. synthetic (rpc-gen) doesn't capture KV cache warming patterns — replay showed a step where p99 spikes after many unique contexts.
maya: KV cache behavior: cache misses cause full KV recompute, which inflates tail when batched with other requests because recompute can't be amortized. if microbatch groups mix warm+cold requests tail suffers.
maria: proposal: 3 changes — 1) limit dynamic microbatching to max 8 for interactive route, 2) tweak kernel selector to prefer lower-latency kernels when p95 target is enabled, 3) add a "cache-affinity" microbatcher that groups requests by cache-hit-probability.
sam: sounds reasonable. data needed: profile of per-token compute for fp16 vs int8 kernels at seq_len 512/1024/2048. I have quick numbers: fp16 conv kernel avg token 0.9ms, int8-gemm 0.6ms when fully batched, but tail for int8 increases by ~2x for single-request path.
li: another datapoint: in replay, cold-cache fraction was ~18% initially, then stabilized ~6% after warmup. the spike correlated with rare long sequences that forced kernel path change.
maya: for benchmark methodology — we should produce three artifacts before changing heuristics: A) real-traffic replay with warmup + long-tail sampling, B) synthetic adversarial generator to produce cache-mix variance, C) microbenchmark for kernel latencies (per-layer, per-seqlen).
maria: agree. product SLOs require p95 300ms for interactive. propose a temporary canary rollback of dynamic-microbatching and release kernel-selector tweak behind feature flag.
sam: I'm worried rollback reduces throughput for batch customers. recommend flag scoped to route-level: interactive vs batch. that avoids global perf regress.
li: also add p99 alerting for route-level — current infra only reports cluster p95. p99 alerts would have fired earlier.
perf-bot: benchmark-report summary attached in thread: https://dash.redwood/bench/1710624000
maria: next steps: sam to produce kernel microbench (numbers by EOD), li to add p99 per-route alert and run replay, maya to prototype cache-affinity microbatcher in a branch, I'll coordinate canary toggles.
sam: noted — will run fp16 vs int8 kernels across seq_len 256/512/1024 with batch sizes [1,4,8,16].
li: will run two replay flavors: full-prod anonymized replay + synthetic cold-hit spike test.
maya: will draft microbatcher design: grouping by KV-cache-hash prefix and a timeout bucket to avoid head-of-line blocking.
maria: timeline: try to get data in 48h, target patch next week. if p95 improves we can enable experimental feature flag for canary.
sam: one more: we need to capture tail-latency distributions (not just p95/p99) — upload histograms (t-digest) so we can compare shapes between runs.
li: yes — ops will wire t-digest export to perf pipeline.
maria: thanks all. syncing in #eng-runtime later today 3pm to review numbers.
maya: :thumbsup:
perf-bot: deploy-checks: canary passed health checks at 1710624100, but tail-latency > threshold.
sam: adding a quick snippet for microbench harness:
```
for bs in [1,4,8,16]:
  run_benchmark(model='redwood-2', seq_len=1024, batch=bs, kernel_pref=['fp16','int8'])
```
maria: perfect — tag me when artifacts are uploaded.
